content.overview: Dividend may be declared only out of profits of the year, or accumulated profits, or both, after providing for depreciation, or out of money provided by the Government, subject to the reserve and deposit rules.
content.glance: Dividend may be declared only out of profits of the year, or accumulated profits, or both, after providing for depreciation, or out of money provided by the Government, subject to the reserve and deposit rules.
content.study: Section 123 is the source rule for dividend. Depreciation under Schedule II must be provided. The company may transfer such percentage as it considers appropriate to reserves. Interim dividend may be declared from surplus in the profit and loss account or from current-year profits. Dividend, including interim dividend, is to be deposited in a scheduled bank in a separate account within five days of declaration. It must be paid or the warrant posted within thirty days under s. 127, failing which the company and directors face consequences, with the exceptions in s. 127. Dividend cannot be declared from unrealised gains or revaluation reserves. A company in default of deposits cannot declare dividend during the default.

examples.title: Revaluation
examples.body: An upward revaluation is not a fund for dividend.

examples.title: Five-day account
examples.body: Declared dividend must move to a separate scheduled-bank account within five days.

distinctions: Declaration is s. 123. Unpaid dividend transfer to the unpaid account and Investor Education and Protection Fund is ss 124-125. Bonus shares are s. 63, not dividend.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can interim dividend be paid from previous-year losses if the current quarter is profitable?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Interim dividend must fit the source rules in s. 123, including the current-profit and no-loss conditions stated in the section. A loss in the preceding quarter restricts the rate.
